b_malayagiri.etymology_analysis: Sanskrit/Odia Malayagiri ('Malaya mountain'), directly adopting the proper name of the prominent peak in the Garhjat Range of Angul district, Odisha.

b_khinjali.first_mention_attestation: Mid-8th century CE (c. 750–800 CE; Sonepur copper-plate grant of Bhanja king Satrubhanja I, son of Silabhanja I)
b_khinjali.etymology_analysis: Sanskrit Khinjali-Mandala ('province of Khinjali'), the early medieval principality of the Bhanja dynasty centered in the Boudh-Phulbani-Sonepur region, attested in 8th-century CE copper plates.

b_nilamadhav.first_mention_attestation: Temple/shrine name at Kantilo, Nayagarh district, Odisha, with no datable pre-867 CE written attestation
b_nilamadhav.etymology_analysis: Sanskrit/Odia Nilamadhava ('blue Madhava'), a manifestation of Vishnu worshipped at the Nilamadhav Temple in Kantilo on the Mahanadi River.

b_nayagarh.first_mention_attestation: c. 1480–1510 CE (reputed foundation of Baghua Nayagarh by local chieftain Baghel Singh)
b_nayagarh.etymology_analysis: Odia/Indo-Aryan Nayagarh ('new fort'), the capital of the former Nayagarh State founded in the late 15th century CE.

b_viraja.first_mention_attestation: 865 CE (Dhauli cave inscription of Bhauma-Kara king Santikaradeva, year 93, naming Bhatta Loyomaka of Viraja, alongside Bhauma-Kara copper plates)
b_viraja.etymology_analysis: Sanskrit Viraja ('pure, free from passion', and name of the presiding goddess Viraja/Biraja), the ancient name of Jajpur in Odisha, attested in Bhauma-Kara epigraphs by 865 CE.

b_ratnagiri.first_mention_attestation: 8th–9th century CE (monastic clay seals and stone/terracotta inscriptions from the Ratnagiri Mahavihara in Jajpur district, Odisha)
b_ratnagiri.etymology_analysis: Sanskrit Ratnagiri ('hill of jewels'), the major Buddhist monastic complex (mahavihara) in Odisha's Diamond Triangle active from the 5th–6th centuries CE and epigraphically attested in 8th–9th century CE seals and inscriptions.

b_bhadrak.first_mention_attestation: Modern/medieval town name derived from Goddess Bhadrakali with no datable pre-867 CE written attestation (the 3rd-century CE Bhadrak inscription of Gana records Panida)
b_bhadrak.etymology_analysis: Odia toponym Bhadrak, derived from the presiding deity Bhadrakali (whose shrine lies near the town).

older_name_by_867.first_mention_source: Bhadrak stone inscription of Mahārāja Gaṇa (c. 3rd century CE)
older_name_by_867.notes: The 3rd-century CE Bhadrak inscription of Gaṇa records the locality/administrative unit Panida prior to the medieval/modern name Bhadrak.

b_baleshvara.first_mention_attestation: Post-medieval coastal town name (anglicized Balasore; English factory established 1634 CE) with no datable pre-867 CE attestation
b_baleshvara.etymology_analysis: Odia Baleswara / Baleshvara (anglicized Balasore), regionally derived from Baneswara (Shiva), the presiding deity of Puruna Baleswar.

b_raibania.first_mention_attestation: 13th century CE (c. 1238–1264 CE; fort complex built during the reign of Eastern Ganga ruler Narasimhadeva I, later recorded in the Ain-i-Akbari)
b_raibania.etymology_analysis: Odia Raibania, the medieval fort complex in Balasore district built under Eastern Ganga king Narasimhadeva I (13th century CE).

b_kodalaka.first_mention_attestation: c. 839 CE (copper-plate inscriptions of Sulki ruler Ranastambha and the Sulki dynasty of Kodalaka Mandala)
b_kodalaka.etymology_analysis: Sanskrit Kodalaka-Mandala ('province of Kodalaka', modern Kualo in Dhenkanal district, Odisha), the 9th-century CE principality of the Sulki feudatories under the Bhauma-Karas.

b_bajrakot.first_mention_attestation: Modern/medieval village name in Angul district, Odisha, with no datable pre-867 CE written attestation
b_bajrakot.etymology_analysis: Odia/Sanskrit Bajrakot ('thunderbolt fort'), a village in Angul district, Odisha, known for the medieval Bhringesvara Shiva temple.

b_deogarh.first_mention_attestation: Modern/early modern town name (Debagarh, former capital of Bamra State) with no datable pre-867 CE written attestation
b_deogarh.etymology_analysis: Odia/Indo-Aryan Deogarh / Debagarh ('fort of the gods'), the former capital of the Bamanda (Bamra) princely state in northwestern Odisha.

b_puri.first_mention_attestation: Late 11th century CE (c. 1078 CE; Prabodha Chandrodaya Nataka mentions Purushottama shrine, and Anantavarman Chodaganga began the Jagannath Temple; shortened to Puri from Purushottama Puri)
b_puri.etymology_analysis: Sanskrit/Odia Puri ('the city'), shortened from Purushottama Puri ('city of Purushottama / Jagannath').

b_ganjam.first_mention_attestation: Early modern town/district name (Potagarh fort built 1768 CE) with no datable pre-867 CE attestation of the form Ganjam
b_ganjam.etymology_analysis: Odia Ganjam, derived either from Persian ganj ('granary, market') or as a later evolution of the 7th-century CE regional name Kongoda.

older_name_by_867.first_mention_source: Ganjam copper-plate grant of Shailodbhava ruler Madhavaraja II (620 CE)
older_name_by_867.notes: The Ganjam region was known as Kongoda (Kangoda) under the Shailodbhava dynasty in the 7th century CE, attested in the 620 CE Ganjam grant.

b_gopalpur.first_mention_attestation: Modern coastal town name (Gopalpur-on-Sea) in Ganjam district, Odisha, with no datable pre-867 CE written attestation
b_gopalpur.etymology_analysis: Sanskrit/Odia Gopalpur ('town of Gopal/Krishna'), a historic coastal port in Ganjam district, Odisha.

b_rayapura.first_mention_attestation: c. 1400 CE (Raipur stone inscription of Kalachuri ruler Brahmadeva of the Raipur branch, late 14th to early 15th century CE)
b_rayapura.eponym_details: Traditionally named after Brahmdeo Rai (Brahmadeva), the late 14th- to early 15th-century CE Kalachuri ruler of the Raipur branch (son of Ramachandra).
b_rayapura.etymology_analysis: Sanskrit/Chhattisgarhi Rayapura ('city of Rai', modern Raipur), capital of the Raipur Kalachuri branch established in the late 14th to early 15th century CE.

b_shivapura.first_mention_attestation: Generic Sanskritized settlement name in Dakshina Kosala / Chhattisgarh with no datable pre-867 CE written attestation
b_shivapura.etymology_analysis: Sanskrit Shivapura ('city of Shiva'), a generic temple-town designation in the Dakshina Kosala region.

b_camparanya.first_mention_attestation: 1479 CE (birthplace of Vaishnava saint Vallabhacharya; formerly known as Champajhar)
b_camparanya.etymology_analysis: Sanskrit Champaranya ('forest of champa flowers'), modern Champaran in Raipur district, Chhattisgarh, famed as the 1479 CE birthplace of Vallabhacharya.
